attacks.q: What does HB 2 from the 2025 regular session cost, according to its fiscal note?
attacks.answer:
The fiscal note for HB 2 from the 2025 regular session (89R) indicates changes related to the Basic Allotment and Guaranteed Yield in the education funding formula. Specifically, it sets the Guaranteed Yield Increment Adjustment at $55 for the 2026-27 biennium, which increases the Basic Allotment from $6,160 to $6,215 in fiscal year 2026. The bill provides additional state aid related to these adjustments.

The fiscal note details are in this source: ftp://ftp.legis.state.tx.us/bills/89R/fiscalnotes/html/house_bills/HB00001_HB00099/HB00002F.htm

No specific total cost figure was extracted from the snippet, but the focus is on adjustments to education funding formulas and state aid. If you want, I can try to find a more precise cost figure.

attacks.q: Explain the fiscal impact of SB 4 from 2025 on the state.
attacks.answer:
SB 4 from the 2025 session has no fiscal cost to the state. The Legislative Budget Board recommends repealing this bill.

Summary:
- The bill amends certain sections of the Tax Code related to Project Finance Zones.
- It allows certain municipalities to designate contiguous geographic areas as Project Finance Zones.
- The bill does not impose any cost on the state budget.

Source: ftp://ftp.legis.state.tx.us/bills/89R/fiscalnotes/html/house_bills/HB02300_HB02399/HB02313F.htm (89R)

attacks.q: Which agencies are affected by HB 9 (2025 regular session)?
attacks.answer:
The agency affected by HB 9 (89R) is the Comptroller of Public Accounts (agency code 304).

- HB 9 relates to an exemption from ad valorem taxation of a portion of the appraised value of tangible personal property held or used for the production of income.
- The bill was enacted in the 2025 regular session.
- The fiscal note indicates a two-year net impact to General Revenue of -$193.50 million (negative).
- The bill was filed on 2025-02-24, passed the House on 2025-04-03, passed the Senate on 2025-05-14, and signed on 2025-06-12.
- The House committee was Ways & Means, and the Senate committee was Local Government.

Source: ftp://ftp.legis.state.tx.us/bills/89R/fiscalnotes/html/house_bills/HB00001_HB00099/HB00009F.htm
